requirement:
`verify` always captures `Some(criterion.version())`. When `load_evidence` loads
an older answer with no known version, `Fingerprinted::version()` returns `None`.
`Record::version` holds the same optional value. In the serialized `revision`
field, a concrete string represents `Some(version)` and `"*"` represents `None`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each clause of `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.recorded_criterion_version`.

- **`verify` always captures `Some(criterion.version())`.**
  - `tests/contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]` asserts that `value.version().unwrap().as_str() == "v1"` after `verify`. It also asserts that the version is preserved after `store_evidence` and `load_evidence`.
  - `tests/contracts.rs#fn[typed_loading_reports_decode_errors_even_for_stale_evidence]` verifies a criterion with revision "v2" and asserts that `value.version()` is "v2". It also asserts that the stored record still has "v1" until the new value is saved.
  - `tests/contracts.rs#fn[concurrent_same_criterion_executions_keep_complete_independent_records]` checks that the stored record's version is the revision of the execution that was saved ("first-revision" or "second-revision").

- **`load_evidence` of an older answer returns `None` from `Fingerprinted::version()`.** `tests/contracts.rs#fn[wildcard_revision_does_not_supply_other_criteria_or_nodes]` sets the stored record's version to `None`. It then loads the record and asserts `loaded.version() == None`. It also asserts that the loaded value is compatible with a different current revision.

- **`Record::version` holds the same optional value, and the `revision` field encodes it.**
  - `tests/storage.rs#fn[record_preserves_the_stored_version_encoding]` deserializes a record from a concrete string such as "review-v1". It asserts `Some("review-v1")` and that re-serialization round-trips to the same wire JSON.
  - The same test does this for `"*"`, asserting `None` and an identical round trip.
  - It also asserts that `CriterionVersion` itself rejects "*".

The only paths not tested directly are re-storing a loaded `None`-version value and `verify` producing `None`. The requirement says `verify` never produces `None`. Writing `None` as "*" is covered by the serialization round trip. No unacknowledged gaps remain, and all tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.
